dod_cost.note: The Pentagon's own estimate, submitted to Congress's defense oversight panels and the highest official figure to date: $11.2bn already obligated for operations plus $32.4bn in unfunded replacement costs for munitions, damaged aircraft and other assets. It excludes damage to US facilities in eight Middle East countries. The Pentagon document itself is not public; the figure is as reported by Roll Call, hence Tier 2.

cbo_estimate.interceptor_finding: The US has probably used between one-half and two-thirds of its inventory of certain interceptors since June 2025; rebuilding those inventories would probably take at least five years.
cbo_estimate.note: CBO's independent estimate, not the Pentagon's. The $1.9bn counts only hardware the department would have to change its plans to replace; replacing everything with platforms available today would cost $3.3bn. CBO notes a Pentagon Inspector General total of $33.4bn through 30 June, consistent with its own once two further months at about $3bn are added. Figures here are as reported by Breaking Defense; the CBO PDF could not be retrieved to check line by line, hence Tier 2 for the breakdown.

Shown as a reported alternative next to the official 18, with the denial; the headline number stays the official count.

aircraft.note: Three F-15Es were lost to friendly fire over Kuwait on 2 March; five KC-135s were damaged on the ground at Prince Sultan Air Base on 14 March; two MC-130Js were destroyed in Iran during the 5 April rescue. Count is as of the CRS report and will be updated from any later official tally. UPDATE 23 Sep 2026: CBO (15 Sep) also counts 42 planes plus one radar system lost through 1 August, so the headline 42 stands. The DoD Lead Inspector General's quarterly report on Operation Epic Fury (released 9 Sep, covering to 30 Jun) gives 'as many as 30' MQ-9s destroyed (CRS: 24) and adds four AH-6s, an AH-64 and an MH-60S not in the CRS list; its counts are 'at least' / 'as many as' ranges, so by_type is NOT changed to mix the two sources (Al Jazeera, 15 Sep, summarising the IG report; IG report https://media.defense.gov/2026/Sep/09/2003993626/-1/-1/1/OEF_Q3_JUN2026_FINAL_508%20SECURE.PDF).

bases.note: Iran struck the Navy's Bahrain logistics hub on the first day. Regional ports large enough for a carrier remain inside missile range, so supply ships sail to Diego Garcia and the fleet resupplies at sea every five to six days. USS Abraham Lincoln spent about nine months deployed without a port call before USS George Washington relieved it on 20 August.
bases.source: Washington Post (228 structures); Stars and Stripes; Defense News

munitions.denial: Defense Secretary Hegseth disputed the reports (5 August); the President demanded answers on the shortages (3 September).
munitions.note: CSIS estimated roughly a third of Patriot interceptors remained as of 27 July and that rebuilding to pre-war levels would take at least three years. CNN reported about 80% of THAAD and half of Patriot stocks used. The $21bn munitions line in the supplemental is consistent with the estimates the Secretary disputes. No newer Tier 1/2 Patriot count found as of 23 Sep. CBO (15 Sep) separately estimates the US has probably used between one-half and two-thirds of its inventory of certain interceptors since June 2025 and that rebuilding would probably take at least five years (see war_cost.cbo_estimate).
munitions.source: CSIS analysis, 27 July 2026; CNN; Stars and Stripes 5 Aug; Axios 3 Sep

fed_counterpoint.name: Why gold did not actually overtake Treasuries as the world's favourite reserve asset
fed_counterpoint.author: Colin Weiss, Federal Reserve Board
fed_counterpoint.finding: The crossover is a valuation effect driven by private ETF demand since late 2024, not central bank accumulation; by June 2026 foreign official Treasury holdings again exceeded world gold reserves excluding the US in dollar terms. Five legacy holders (US, Germany, Italy, France, IMF) own 52% of official gold and have not added since the 1970s. Foreign officials bought roughly USD 200bn of Treasuries net between 2022 and April 2026.
